questions.prompt: A field guide says a coral reef has far more biodiversity than the same area of Arctic tundra, comparing them at the species level. What does biodiversity describe here?
questions.accessiblePrompt: A field guide says a coral reef has far more biodiversity than the same area of Arctic tundra, comparing them at the species level. What does biodiversity describe here?

choices.text: The variety of life there, counted as different kinds of organisms
choices.rationale: Correct. Biodiversity means the variety of life. Here the level being compared is species, so a place with more different species has more biodiversity.

choices.text: How many individual organisms live there in all
choices.rationale: That is abundance, not variety. A field packed with millions of plants of a single crop has huge numbers but very little biodiversity.

choices.text: How much all the living things there weigh together
choices.rationale: That is biomass. Producers hold most of Earth's living mass, yet they are less than a quarter of named species, so mass and variety are different measurements.

choices.text: How much water, sunlight and other nonliving resources are found there
choices.rationale: Water and sunlight are nonliving factors. They help explain why some places hold more species, but they are not biodiversity itself.

questions.conditions: Level compared: species (how many different kinds of organisms live in a place).
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of life. It can be compared at several levels, such as the variety of genes within a species, of species, or of whole ecosystems, so a good comparison says which level it uses. This lesson compares species: more kinds of organisms means more biodiversity, whatever the total number or weight of living things.
questions.misconception: Biodiversity means how many organisms live somewhere, or how much living material is there.
questions.hint: Think about what the word diversity means: a variety of what?

evidence.locator: Vocabulary box; Section 1. The Importance of Biodiversity
evidence.supports: Biodiversity is the variety of organisms on Earth or in a particular habitat or ecosystem, and each ecosystem has its own natural set of species.
